previous_disclosures.summary: Data Center revenue for fiscal year 2023 was $15.01 billion, up 41% from fiscal year 2022, driven by hyperscaler and cloud usage of accelerated computing platforms and networking. The company announced the NVIDIA Hopper GPU architecture and began ramping products like the H100 Tensor Core GPU, launched the NVIDIA OVX server reference design, completed two new large language models (NeMo LLM and BioNeMo LLM), and announced the Spectrum-4 networking platform while shipping Quantum-2.

comparisons.peer_summary: Data Center net revenue increased 94% to $12.6 billion in 2024 from $6.5 billion in 2023, primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs. Operating income rose to $3.5 billion in 2024 from $1.3 billion in 2023, mainly due to higher revenue partially offset by increased R&D investment.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD reported substantial year-over-year growth in their Data Center segments for fiscal year 2024, attributing the increases to demand for AI accelerators and processors. NVDA reported Data Center revenue of $47.5 billion, a 217% increase, with approximately 40% attributed to AI inference. AMD reported Data Center net revenue of $12.6 billion, a 94% increase, driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and EPYC CPUs. While NVDA emphasized the inference portion and specific platform launches (Spectrum-X, DGX Cloud), AMD highlighted the dual driver of GPU and CPU sales alongside a significant rise in operating income to $3.5 billion.

sentences.text: Data Center revenue for fiscal year 2024 was $47.5 billion, up 217% from fiscal year 2023.
We estimate that in fiscal year 2024, approximately 40% of Data Center revenue was for AI inference.
Data Center net revenue of $12.6 billion in 2024 increased by 94%, compared to net revenue of $6.5 billion in 2023.
Data Center operating income was $3.5 billion in 2024, compared to operating income of $1.3 billion in 2023.
